findings.message: 'API_TOKEN' is assigned a literal credential-looking string
findings.why: a literal credential is copied into every clone, backup and CI log; rotating it means shipping code, so in practice it never gets rotated.
findings.suggestion: read it from os.environ / a secret manager and rotate this value

findings.message: 'sql' builds a SQL string by interpolation
findings.why: concatenating values into SQL lets input change the query's meaning (dropping tables or reading other tenants' rows) instead of its data.
findings.suggestion: keep the statement constant and pass values as parameters

findings.message: SQL statement is assembled from a runtime value
findings.why: concatenating values into SQL lets input change the query's meaning (dropping tables or reading other tenants' rows) instead of its data.
findings.suggestion: use a parameterised query: execute(sql, (value,))

findings.message: use of eval() on a runtime value is a code-injection sink
findings.why: eval/exec compile attacker-controlled text into live code; one unescaped input turns a data bug into remote code execution.
findings.suggestion: replace with ast.literal_eval() or an explicit dispatch dict

findings.message: subprocess called with shell=True
findings.why: shell=True hands the string to /bin/sh, so any ';' or '$(...)' in an interpolated value runs as a second command with your privileges.
findings.suggestion: pass an argument list (['git', 'clone', url]) and drop shell=True

findings.message: os.system() executes through the shell
findings.why: os.system() always goes through the shell and gives you no way to pass arguments safely, so every call site is a potential injection point.
findings.suggestion: use subprocess.run([...], shell=False) and check returncode

findings.message: module imports 13 distinct top-level modules (max 12)
findings.why: a module importing many others must be rebuilt, retested and redeployed whenever any of them changes.
findings.suggestion: split the module by responsibility so each part has few dependencies

findings.message: 'build_report' nests control flow 6 levels deep (max 4)
findings.why: each nesting level multiplies the conditions a reader must track; deeply nested code is where inverted-condition bugs live.
findings.suggestion: invert conditions to return early, or extract the inner loop

findings.message: 'build_report' cyclomatic complexity 21 (max 10)
findings.why: cyclomatic complexity is the number of independent paths; past ~10 the function cannot be covered by tests or held in a reviewer's head.
findings.suggestion: extract the branch bodies into named helpers and use early returns

findings.message: 'build_report' is 65 lines (max 60)
findings.why: a function longer than a screen cannot be diffed or reviewed as a unit, so changes to it are approved without being understood.
findings.suggestion: split it along its comment headings into separate functions

findings.message: configuration key 'stripe_secret_key' holds a literal credential
findings.why: a literal credential is copied into every clone, backup and CI log; rotating it means shipping code, so in practice it never gets rotated.
findings.suggestion: move the value to a secret manager, reference it by name, and rotate it

findings.message: 'normalize_status' returns a value on some paths and falls through to an implicit None on others
findings.why: some paths return a value and others fall off the end returning None, so callers crash on attribute access for a subset of inputs.
findings.suggestion: add a final `return` with an explicit value, or raise

findings.message: function 'collect_errors' has a mutable default argument
findings.why: the default object is created once at def time and shared by every call, so state leaks between unrelated callers.
findings.suggestion: default to None and build the container inside the function

findings.message: `is` used to compare against the literal 'USD'
findings.why: `is` compares identity, and equal literals are only sometimes the same object (interning), so the comparison works in tests and fails in prod.
findings.suggestion: use == / != for value comparison; keep `is` for None

findings.message: pickle.loads() rebuilds arbitrary objects from untrusted bytes
findings.why: pickle/marshal/yaml.load reconstruct arbitrary objects, which executes code chosen by whoever produced the byte stream.
findings.suggestion: use json, or verify an HMAC over the payload before loading

findings.message: assert validates argument(s) of 'validate_amount'
findings.why: asserts are stripped under `python -O`, so validation written as an assert silently disappears in optimised production builds.
findings.suggestion: raise ValueError(...) so the check survives `python -O`

findings.message: 'flatten_rows' is 89% structurally identical to 'expand_records' at utils/helpers.py:4
findings.why: copy-pasted logic means every bug must be fixed N times; in practice only the copy that was reported gets fixed.
findings.suggestion: extract the shared logic into one function and call it from both sites

findings.message: statement is unreachable: the preceding return always exits this block
findings.why: unreachable code is never executed or tested, so it rots and then misleads the next reader into believing it runs.
findings.suggestion: delete it, or move it above the exit statement

findings.message: 'build_report' takes 8 parameters (max 6)
findings.why: long parameter lists are positional-argument bugs waiting to happen and signal that the function owns several responsibilities.
findings.suggestion: group the related ones into a dataclass or config object

findings.message: public function 'flatten_rows' lacks a docstring
findings.why: public API without a docstring forces every caller to read the implementation, and makes intent-vs-behaviour bugs unprovable.
findings.suggestion: document what it returns and which errors it raises

findings.message: module has no docstring
findings.why: public API without a docstring forces every caller to read the implementation, and makes intent-vs-behaviour bugs unprovable.
findings.suggestion: add a one-line module docstring describing its responsibility

findings.message: import 'hashlib' is never used
findings.why: dead imports slow start-up, create phantom dependencies and hide which modules are really coupled.
findings.suggestion: remove the import

findings.message: # TODO: delete this module once the v2 exporter ships
findings.why: a TODO in code is an issue nobody is tracking and nobody is assigned.
findings.suggestion: file an issue and link it, or delete the note

findings.why: a private helper nobody calls is dead weight that still has to be read, understood and kept compiling.
findings.suggestion: delete it, or make it public if other modules need it
